title: Winter Laundry Room Organization: Where to Put Bulky Sweaters, Blankets and Wet Snow Gear
description: Bulky sweaters, heavy blankets and wet snow gear? An easy winter laundry room setup for busy brains, plus 7 Amazon finds for drying and storage.
intro:
Winter laundry is a different beast. The loads are bigger. Sweaters can't go in the dryer. Snow pants are soaked. And that giant comforter barely fits in the machine, let alone anywhere else.

So the laundry room fills up with things that are half wet, half dry and fully in the way. And when the space feels chaotic, we put off laundry even longer.

Here's how to set up the laundry room for winter in small steps, so the bulky stuff has somewhere to go. Plus seven Amazon finds that make drying, sorting and storing easier.

sections.heading: Make a 'hang to dry' spot first
sections.body:
This is the biggest winter problem. Sweaters, leggings and snow gear can't go in the dryer, so they end up draped over chairs all over the house.

Give them one spot. A folding drying rack, a retractable clothesline or a tension rod over the tub works. Put it as close to the washer as you can, so wet clothes go straight from the machine to the rack.

sections.heading: Dry snow gear separately
sections.body:
Wet mittens, hats and snow pants need their own drying zone, ideally right by the door. A boot dryer or a few hooks above a tray keeps the drips in one place.

If gear dries overnight, it's ready for the morning. No more hunting for the second mitten at 7:45 a.m.

sections.heading: Sort bulky loads before they start
sections.body:
Winter laundry has more "special" loads: delicate sweaters, heavy towels, blankets. Use a divided hamper or a couple of labeled bins so things are sorted as they're tossed in.

When a bin is full, that's a load. No sorting on laundry day, no big pile on the floor.

sections.heading: Wash one big thing at a time
sections.body:
Comforters and heavy blankets fill the washer fast. Pick one day a month as "big blanket day" and wash one item. Add two dryer balls to help it dry faster and keep it from bunching up.

If it doesn't fit in your machine, that's what a laundromat's big washers are for. One trip, all the blankets, done in an hour.

sections.heading: Store extra blankets where you use them
sections.body: Extra blankets don't need to live in the laundry room. Store them in a basket by the couch or under the bed in a zip storage bag. They're out of the way, and they're right there on cold nights.

sections.heading: Use the space above the machines
sections.body: Most laundry rooms have empty wall space above the washer and dryer. A shelf or a slim rolling cart beside the machines holds detergent, dryer balls and stain spray. Keep it simple: the stuff you use every load stays in reach, everything else goes up high.

finds.name: Folding clothes drying rack
finds.search: collapsible clothes drying rack for laundry
finds.why: Gives sweaters and leggings one spot to dry instead of every chair in the house. Folds flat when you're done.

finds.name: Retractable indoor clothesline
finds.why: Pulls out when you need it and disappears when you don't. Great for small laundry rooms.

finds.name: Divided laundry hamper
finds.why: Sort as you toss: sweaters, towels, everything else. A full section means it's time for a load.

finds.name: Wool dryer balls
finds.why: Toss a few in with heavy blankets. They help bulky loads dry more evenly and with less bunching.

finds.name: Boot and glove dryer
finds.search: boot and glove dryer for winter gear
finds.why: Wet boots and mittens dry overnight, so they're ready in the morning instead of soggy.

finds.name: Slim rolling laundry cart
finds.search: slim rolling storage cart for laundry room
finds.why: Slides into the gap beside the washer and holds detergent and stain spray right where you need them.

finds.name: Zippered blanket storage bags
finds.search: zippered blanket storage bags with clear window
finds.why: Keeps extra blankets clean under the bed, with a window so you can see which one is which.

outro:
Winter laundry feels heavier because it literally is. Give bulky and wet things their own spots, and the laundry room stops being a pile you avoid.

If laundry is always the chore that falls behind, *The Messy Brain Home Reset* has a full laundry loop made for brains that forget the washer.
